DefiLlama's Intents volume changes meaning on 2026-09-01. From 2026-04-01 to 2026-08-31 it matches NearBlocks' public-only figure within 0.2% (see intents_volume_2026_apr_aug_defillama_vs_nearblocks), and from 2026-09-01 it equals revenue.near.org's all-routes figure, which includes confidential Intents. Its adapter carries no date rule, so the likely cause is that DefiLlama kept its stored daily values when NEAR restated the earlier months; that is not confirmed. So all-route volume is taken from revenue.near.org and public volume from NearBlocks, and DefiLlama's series is used only in this comparison. Its fees change scope the same way, through 2026-09-13.

Both figures are retired, and they were never independent. NearBlocks computed circulating supply from lockup contracts until its 2025-09-03 rewrite removed that job, so /v1/charts and /v1/stats have read 1,249,836,992 NEAR since 2025-08-27. CoinMetrics takes project-reported supply through CoinGecko, and NEAR's report is NearBlocks' legacy endpoint: the two stayed within 0.02% (median) from November 2024, CoinMetrics carried the frozen figure for two months, and on 2025-10-25, two days after NearBlocks pointed that endpoint at total supply, it jumped to total supply and has followed the previous day's total ever since. Circulating supply is now built from the lockup contracts on chain.

The Launch row differs by design. NEAR's post warns that unclaimed tokens, over 300M at the time, sat in unlocked accounts until claimed, so the chain shows more unlocked than the plan until those lockups were made in the following weeks. NearBlocks' figure for that day is within 0.03% of the chain-built one. The later rows stay within 5%: the plan assumes full issuance and no burning, and lockups kept being created after launch.

Only 2024 differs, and the fault is NearBlocks'. From 2024-08-12 its job counted a lockup it failed to read three times as nothing locked, so RPC failures pushed its figure as high as 99.95% of total supply. Its commit of 2024-11-04 made such a failure stop the job instead, so the figure stood still until 2024-12-28. Outside that window the two are close every day, and a test checks that they stay so.

Two definitions, not an error. GitHub's weekly statistic counts commits beyond the default branch: near/nearcore keeps release branches, and a sweep of one week found commits on 2.14-release. The commits list, the search API and GraphQL's history all give the default-branch count. The statistic runs below the default branch for other repositories (ton-blockchain/ton, near/near-api-js) and returns a year of zeros for anza-xyz/agave, so the default-branch count is used for every repository.

Expected: the burn figure is a lower bound, and this is the one place it can be measured. Before issuance began on 2020-10-20 nothing was minted, so every fall in total supply was gas burned. Over those 79 days supply fell by 124.4 NEAR against gas fees of 146.8 NEAR, which is 84.8% of gas, while the burn figure takes 70%. The contracts' share was 30% of the gas burnt executing function calls, not of all gas, so the real burn was always more than 70% of the fee and never more than all of it. The lower bound held on every one of the 79 days, and a test keeps it so. The 84.8% belongs to 2020's mix of transactions, so it is not applied to later years; treat the burn figure before 2026-11-04 as a floor. From that day protocol version 87 burns all gas and the figure is exact.

The chain side is NEAR that moved into or out of the listed wallets after the seed day; the fund side is each day's change in shares times the NEAR behind one share. On the days of 1 to 9 October the split between days was itself taken from the chain, but the total to 12 October comes from reported totals, so the two sums are independent. A gap that grows would mean NEAR arrives or leaves outside the wallets Bitwise lists.
A day outside the range would mean the NAV, the NEAR in trust or the share count on Bitwise's page does not fit the market that day.
